resources.string: Let duit-log see your Wallet notifications

duit-log logs your spending from the notifications Touch \'n Go eWallet, Grab and Shopee show after each payment. To read them it needs notification access. Android has no way to give an app only some apps\' notifications, so this permission covers every notification on the phone.

duit-log drops every notification that isn\'t from Touch \'n Go eWallet, Grab or Shopee the moment it arrives: it never saves it, logs it or sends it anywhere. Everything duit-log keeps stays on this phone, and its code is open for anyone to check.

Android 13 and later block notification access for apps installed from outside the Play Store. Open App info, tap ⋮ in the top corner, then \"Allow restricted settings\", and confirm. If the option isn\'t there, do step 2 first: it appears once Android has blocked the switch, or never, if your phone doesn\'t restrict duit-log.

duit-log already ignores other apps: it drops every notification that isn\'t from Touch \'n Go eWallet, Grab or Shopee without reading it. If you want Android to stop passing their notifications at all, open \"Apps\" (on some phones \"See all apps\") on duit-log\'s notification access page and switch them off there. At least consider messaging, banking, SMS and email apps. You can skip this step.
Later versions ask you right after each payment which Category it belongs to, in a notification.
duit-log can\'t see notifications, so it isn\'t recording your Wallet payments. Turn notification access back on.
Records every notification from Touch \'n Go eWallet, Grab and Shopee, and nothing else, so their wording can be used to read payments later.
The recordings are full, so new notifications aren\'t being recorded. Share them, then clear them.
